patches.value: Let J=[r/2,3r/2] and choose compact C from H003. To cover the allowed empty-C case, set C*=C∪{0}; this is compact and nonempty, and u=q outside C* throughout J because outside C* implies outside C. Thus the derivative fields, including e_t, vanish outside C*. By M005, C*×J is compact and nonempty. M004 applied to continuous e_t gives uniform continuity on C*×J. Choose δ>0 so points within δ have e_t values differing by less than 1; the δ/2-balls centered at all points of C*×J cover it, and compactness gives a finite subcover with at least one center p_i. Therefore K=1+max_i |e_t(p_i)| is a well-defined finite nonnegative bound for |e_t| on C*×J. Off C*, e_t=0, so |e_t(x,τ)|≤K·1_{C*}(x) for every x and τ∈J. Since C* is compact, it is measurable and has finite Lebesgue measure; M008 gives integrability on C* of the constant K and M009 gives integrability of b=K·1_{C*} on ℝⁿ. For F(τ)(x)=e(x,τ) and F′(τ)(x)=e_t(x,τ), continuity gives strong measurability, and N001 gives F(r) integrable. Smoothness gives the pointwise parameter derivative; the bound above is uniform in τ∈J. The interval (r/2,3r/2) is a neighborhood of r. Thus the hypotheses of M006 hold and E is differentiable at r with E′(r)=∫e_t(x,r)dx. Since r was arbitrary, this holds for every positive time.
